classification.difficultyReason: Identify opposite rays at a shared vertex and name the resulting vertically opposite angle.

content.prompt: Name the angle that is vertically opposite to $\angle PQR$ in each diagram below.

spec.description: Two crossing straight lines with P–Q–S and T–Q–R collinear.
spec.mathematics: QP and QS are opposite rays; QR and QT are opposite rays.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied point labels are visible.

answer.worked: $QP$ and $QS$ are opposite rays, and $QR$ and $QT$ are opposite rays. Therefore the vertically opposite angle is $\angle SQT$.

spec.description: A nearly vertical line U–Q–R intersects the diagonal V–Q–P.
spec.mathematics: QP and QV are opposite rays; QR and QU are opposite rays.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied point labels are visible.

answer.worked: $QP$ and $QV$ are opposite rays, and $QR$ and $QU$ are opposite rays. Therefore the vertically opposite angle is $\angle VQU$.

spec.description: Rectangle BPRA with both diagonals BR and AP meeting at Q; no additional right-angle or equality marks.
spec.mathematics: QP and QA are opposite rays; QR and QB are opposite rays.
spec.answerVisibility: The rectangle boundary, diagonals and supplied point labels remain visible.

answer.worked: $QP$ and $QA$ are opposite rays, and $QR$ and $QB$ are opposite rays. Therefore the vertically opposite angle is $\angle AQB$.

spec.description: Circle with circumference points P, O, R and N. Chords PN and RO intersect at Q; chords PR and ON are also present. O is a circumference point, not the intersection or centre.
spec.mathematics: QP and QN are opposite rays; QR and QO are opposite rays.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied chords and point labels remain visible; no answer angle is marked.

answer.worked: $QP$ and $QN$ are opposite rays, and $QR$ and $QO$ are opposite rays. Therefore the vertically opposite angle is $\angle NQO$.
